newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: OPTISCAN SHARES LIST AT 30 PCT PREMIUM.
newsitem.headline: OPTISCAN SHARES LIST AT 30 PCT PREMIUM.

text.p: Shares in microscope manufacturer Optiscan Imaging Ltd made their debut on the Australian Stock Exchange at 26 cents, a 30 percent premium to their issue price of 20 cents per share.
The issue raised A$3 million through the issue of 15 million shares with free attaching options.
Shares on issue will total about 48 million, with existing shareholders retaining 69 percent of the company while the public holds 31 percent.
Major shareholders include bioscience investor Circadian Technologies with 15.35 percent.
Optiscan produces confocal microscopes, which differ from ordinary light microscopes in the way in which a laser light is used to illuminate and observe a specimen.
Its major product is currently a desktop confocal microscope, the Optiscan F900e, with a list price of A$90,000.

However, in its prospectus, the company said it was focussing its efforts on developing its confocal endomicroscope which utilises optical fibres, allowing it to be small enough to be inserted into the human body.
The laser and optical fibre based product would allow non-invasive disease monitoring and diagnosis as it would mean living tissue could be examined in-situ at the cellular level, the company said.
Market release of the new product is planned for 1999.
By 11.10 a.m. (0110 GMT), Optiscan shares were at 23 cents, up three cents on the issue price on turnover of 210,00 shares.
